walkthroughs.body_html: Cell 4 runs from Selsey Bill to Beachy Head. Net longshore drift eastward. Chalk recession at Birling Gap reached 1 m/yr 2014-15 storms. Shingle accumulates at Brighton; groyne field maintains beach as defence and tourism asset.

Environment Agency breached 110 m sea wall in 2013, creating 183 ha intertidal habitat. £28 million scheme protects 348 homes from 1-in-1000 year flood. Habitat for migratory birds; oysters returning. Saved £90 million in defence costs over 100 years.

£10 million rock armour and sea wall protects 4500 homes including holiday parks. Bill (point) erodes 2 m/yr unprotected. Loss of Manhood Peninsula (becoming an island) possible without continued investment. Demonstrates value-based defence prioritisation.

mcqs.q: What is the polar jet stream?
options: The three cells are tropical, temperate and arctic, named after climate zones.
The jet stream is a low-level wind that pushes clouds along.
A fast-flowing river of air ~10km up at the boundary between the Ferrel and Polar cells, where large temperature contrasts create strong winds steering weather systems.
The jet stream is the air left behind by aircraft engines.

mcqs.q: Why are there no volcanoes at conservative plate boundaries?
options: There are no volcanoes because the boundaries are too cold.
Conservative boundaries involve plates sliding past each other horizontally — no crust is created or destroyed, so there is no subduction to generate magma.
There are volcanoes at conservative boundaries — that's where most of them form.
The jet stream is the air left behind by aircraft engines.
